candidate.title: 5’-GRO-seq
candidate.scope: The middle, explicitly labelled 5′-GRO-seq row of the assigned Illumina schematic, clarified by the matching Lam et al. 2013 5′-GRO-Seq implementation. The readout is cap-enriched nascent RNA 5′ sequence carried by an amplified cDNA library. The upper BruChase-seq row, lower BruDRB-seq row and right-side chemical legend are surrounding poster context, with no connecting route to this target row. No alternative target workflow is depicted within the assigned row. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete execution protocol or a claim that all GRO-seq variants use this preparation.

The primary implementation starts from prepared nuclei; nuclear preparation is an input interface rather than an extra drawn operation.

states.label: Amplified cDNA library representing capped nascent RNA 5′ ends
features: The terminal blue line is explicitly labelled cDNA; RNA is the biological target and DNA is the sequencing-library carrier.
The intended amplified class derives from RNA with both adaptors, enriching formerly capped BrU-containing 5′ fragments.
The paper uses this readout to localize transcription start sites, including mRNA and enhancer RNA initiation. It does not make this a full-length transcript or steady-state RNA-abundance assay.

Recovery requires a cap-derived fragment that survives fragmentation and label selection. The schematic does not establish exhaustive detection of every initiation event or a quantitative enrichment efficiency.

operations.label: Run-on with analog
operations.description: Engaged nuclear transcription complexes extend nascent RNA using Br-UTP, producing bromouridine-labelled run-on RNA.
operations.mechanism: Br-UTP supplies incorporable bromouridine; the red/orange stars track incorporated label.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a chemical affinity handle into newly extended RNA while retaining its association with nascent transcription. The label alone is not a cap selector.

operations.label: DNase treatment and hydrolyze
operations.description: The run-on RNA preparation is DNase-treated and RNA is hydrolyzed into free fragments, replacing the transcription-complex cartoon with capped, uncapped and unlabelled RNA fragments.
operations.mechanism: DNase removes DNA from the preparation; hydrolysis fragments RNA. Extraction is reported in the primary implementation but is not drawn as a separate operation.
operations.information_effect: Retains BrU and the original cap only on fragments that carry them; loses intact transcript connectivity.

operations.label: Ligate adaptors with truncated mutant RNA ligase 2 and RNA ligase 1
operations.description: The two RNA classes acquire a 3′ adaptor; only the formerly capped class also acquires a 5′ adaptor. Both products are visibly retained in the same reaction mixture.
